issues.legal_issue: A pure question of law may be considered for the first time before the court of last resort when its factual foundation is established and deciding it requires no resolution of disputed factual questions.
material_facts: The argument that subletting one room could justify eviction from all rooms was raised at the final appellate stage, with permission sought and granted to urge additional grounds.
The single tenancy, the different alleged violations in the rooms, and the subletting finding for one room were established or undisputed; deciding the argument required no further factual findings.
issues.conclusion: The court considered the newly raised legal argument because it rested on established facts and raised no factual questions requiring resolution.
issues.legal_principle: A pure question of law can be examined at any stage if its factual foundation has been laid and its legal consequences have not been considered. The court relied on Yeswant Deorao Deshmukh v. Walchand Ramchand Kothari, Connecticut Fire Insurance Co. v. Kavanagh, and Chittoori Subbanna v. Kudappa Subbanna, including the principle that permission to urge additional grounds may be sought by a separate application.

rule.if: final_appellate_proceeding and pure_question_of_law and factual_foundation_established and no_disputed_factual_questions

predicates.final_appellate_proceeding: The matter is before a court exercising final appellate review.
predicates.pure_question_of_law: The issue concerns the legal consequences of established facts rather than a dispute about what happened.
predicates.factual_foundation_established: The facts necessary to assess the legal issue have been established or are undisputed.
predicates.no_disputed_factual_questions: Deciding the issue does not require resolving disputed factual questions.

issues.definition: When a final appellate proceeding presents a pure legal issue based on established facts and requiring no resolution of disputed facts, the issue is considered even if raised late.

issues.legal_issue: Unauthorized subletting of part of a single tenancy may justify eviction from the entire premises covered by that tenancy.
material_facts: The three shop rooms were subject to one tenancy, and a single eviction notice and petition covered all three rooms.
The alleged violations differed among the rooms, but the final findings established unauthorized subletting in one room and not in the others.
The landlords sought eviction under the rent-control law, and the tenants did not obtain an order disturbing the finding of subletting.
issues.conclusion: The landlords were entitled to eviction from the entire premises covered by the single tenancy, even though only part of the premises had been sublet.
issues.legal_principle: Section 11(4)(i) of the Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1965 permits an eviction application where a tenant, without the landlord’s consent and without a lease right to do so, sublets the entire building or any portion of it; its proviso requires registered notice of the contravention and failure to terminate the sublease within thirty days. The court held that subletting any part gives a right to evict from the whole single tenancy. It relied on M. Meeramytheen v. K. Parameswaran Pillai, which applied the same principle to a single tenancy covering multiple shop rooms.

rule.if: rent_control_eviction_case and single_tenancy and unauthorized_subletting_of_part and lease_did_not_authorize_subletting and required_notice_given_and_sublease_not_terminated

predicates.rent_control_eviction_case: The proceeding seeks eviction of a tenant under a rent-control regime.
predicates.single_tenancy: The premises at issue are held under one tenancy, even if they comprise multiple parts or units.
predicates.unauthorized_subletting_of_part: The tenant sublet some part of the premises without the landlord’s consent.
predicates.lease_did_not_authorize_subletting: The lease did not give the tenant a right to sublet the premises or the relevant part.
predicates.required_notice_given_and_sublease_not_t: The landlord gave the required registered notice of the contravention, and the tenant did not terminate the sublease within the required time.

issues.definition: In a rent-control eviction case, if one tenancy covers the premises, the tenant unauthorizedly sublets part without a lease right to do so, and the required notice is not followed by termination of the sublease, eviction may extend to the entire premises covered by that tenancy.
